verdicts.strongest_argument: Every fact that would justify removing the going-concern qualifier is already public and already carried in the price. HSR early termination (8/25), the pull-forward to an end-September close, and the absence of a financing condition are all disclosed in 8-Ks and in the 8/26 timing press release; the $400M/$4.84-per-share net-cash outcome was announced 7/22 and the stock rose ~21% that day. Removing the ASC 205-40 doubt language is a mechanical accounting consequence of those already-known facts, not new information. A stub trading at $3.815 against a stated $4.84 net-cash-at-close is priced on deal-arbitrage math, where a going-concern flag is second-order; the qualifier existed only because of the covenant/forbearance stress that the signed, HSR-cleared, unconditioned deal resolves — and the market already knows the deal resolves it. The 'machine-readable flag, no PR to dilute it' angle is the only genuinely unpriced sliver, plus residual uncertainty over whether management actually removes it in a filing nobody parses in real time.

prior_publication.what_it_says: HSR early-terminated 8/25, close expected by end of September 2026, no financing condition remaining beyond the 20-day notice period.
Signed $400M asset sale to Progress; at close ~$246M net cash or $4.84/share, an 81% premium to 30-day VWAP.
Q1 10-Q carried the substantial-doubt going-concern language tied to the covenant breach and forbearance.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Using spot ($3.815) and the roughly flat 20-day tape (+0.39%), not the 7-event history or the 18% median, which pre-date the transaction and are invalid here. The ~21% discount of spot to the announced $4.84 net-cash figure shows the market has settled the name into a deal-arb range; a going-concern removal that merely confirms known deal progress has little room to move that range. No option chain, so no skew appeal.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If the 10-Q retained the going-concern qualifier (surprise), or if it were shown that a filing-only flag flip on a thin stub reliably moves price, the bullish novelty would rise; I resolved the flat-tape ambiguity toward 'absorbed' because the deal terms are heavily covered and the price sits at a rational arb discount, not at zero.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both load-bearing components are already published. The ~$5.9M of lender/legal fees on the June 12 forbearance effectiveness are disclosed in the June forbearance 8-K and the Q1 10-Q, and the $39.1M 4/30 cash line is in that same Q1 10-Q. The purchase-price-adjustment formula — $400M base minus the amount by which the $25M Minimum Cash Amount exceeds estimated cash, with no upward adjustment for excess cash — is spelled out in the 8/24 DEFM14C, and the 7/22 announcement itself flagged the price as 'subject to customary purchase price adjustments.' So the mechanism that cash burn can cut shareholder proceeds is public, and the 21% discount of spot ($3.815) to the stated $4.84 net-cash figure already prices deal-value uncertainty of this kind. What is genuinely new tonight is only the exact 7/31 cash snapshot, and even that is not the operative measurement — the adjustment is struck at closing (end-September), not at 7/31 — so a single quarter-end balance-sheet line is a waypoint, not the settlement number. The 'narrow corridor' framing is also somewhat overstated: $39.1M less $5.9M is $33.2M before operating burn, comfortably above the $25M floor at quarter start.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Base purchase price ~$400M subject to downward adjustment for the amount by which the $25M Minimum Cash Amount exceeds estimated cash; no upward adjustment for excess cash.
Q1 10-Q reports $39.1M cash at 4/30 and the forbearance-related fees; going-concern context.
Announced $400M price 'subject to customary purchase price adjustments' and $4.84/share net cash estimate.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Using spot and the flat 20-day tape only. Spot sits ~21% below the announced $4.84 net-cash-at-close, a discount wide enough to already embed cash/adjustment and timing risk of the sort this claim describes. No skew or implied move exists (unusable chain), so I cannot see the market pricing downside directly, but the arb discount is the relevant tell and it is already sizeable.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: If tonight's 10-Q showed 7/31 cash materially compressed toward or below $25M — a genuine surprise versus the $33M-ish implied start point — this would be real, unpriced downside and the number should fall sharply; I resolved the flat-tape ambiguity toward 'partly absorbed' because the adjustment formula and fee burn were already public before this print and the arb discount is consistent with that risk being known.

interactions: Source cluster: both findings read the Q1 (4/30) 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001505952/000162828026043173/domo10q-20260430.htm). DOMO#0 cites it directly for the going-concern language; DOMO#1's key figures ($39.1M cash, ~$5.9M forbearance fees) also originate from that same Q1 10-Q, even though DOMO#1 is nominally sourced to the 8/24 DEFM14C. Collapse the Q1-10-Q readings to a single residual. The distinct document in DOMO#1 is the DEFM14C, which is the sole source of the purchase-price-adjustment formula ($25M Minimum Cash Amount, no upward adjustment) — that term is NOT in the Q1 10-Q, so DOMO#1 rests on two documents and only its adjustment-mechanism leg is independent of the Q1-10-Q cluster. The two findings are near-mirrors: DOMO#0 argues the filing removes a negative flag (bullish confirmation of deal progress) while DOMO#1 argues the same filing exposes a cash-proceeds risk; both are ultimately re-readings of already-public deal economics anchored to the 7/22 $4.84/share figure.
